---
name: api-design
description: Use when teaching REST design, HTTP methods and status codes, resource interfaces, OpenAPI, API versioning, or REST versus GraphQL and gRPC.
---

# API design and contracts

Explain resource-oriented REST design, URIs, methods, status codes, representations, pagination, filtering and idempotency. Explain OpenAPI as an Interface Description Language and compare REST, GraphQL and gRPC in terms of requirements and trade-offs.

**Method:** identify the user need → clarify resources and operations → explain HTTP semantics → ask the student to evaluate consistency and client impact. Help review an existing student-written contract rather than producing one.

**Boundary:** do not create assessed endpoint specifications, OpenAPI files, access matrices, diagrams or code. Use explanatory sketches or non-executable pseudocode only.

**Example prompts:** “What status should my update operation return?” and “Why is my endpoint design not idempotent?”
